references.text: The burnt offering (עֹלָה) was to be a male animal without defect, as described in the basic sacrificial laws of Leviticus.
The sin offering (חַטָּאת) is explained in detail here, showing how the priest was to present it before the Lord.
The sin offering and the burnt offering are mentioned together as part of atonement rituals, such as in the Nazirite law.
The priest (הַכֹּהֵן) brings the offering before the face of the Lord, using the same wording found at the conclusion of the Nazirite law.
Earlier in the same chapter, sin offerings and burnt offerings are also mentioned in connection with a Nazirite who has become unclean.
The context for verse 16, where the various offerings the Nazirite must bring are listed in detail.
The Greek New Testament explains that the repeated sacrifices under the law, including sin offerings and burnt offerings, were shadows of the perfect sacrifice in Christ.
